alt: Atom of potassium-39: a nucleus of 19 protons and 20 neutrons (mass number 39) surrounded by 19 electrons in shells of 2, 8, 8 and 1; the numbers of protons and electrons are equal so the atom is neutral.
caption: Figure: the particles in an atom of potassium-39

alt: Paper chromatography: a pencil base line above the solvent level in a covered beaker, and a chromatogram where the solvent front is 8.0 cm above the base line; dye A has moved 3.6 cm (Rf = 0.45), dye B 5.6 cm (Rf = 0.70), and the mixture separates into both spots.
caption: Figure: set-up and chromatogram; Rf = distance moved by the spot ÷ distance moved by the solvent front

alt: Dot-and-cross diagrams: ammonia NH3 has nitrogen sharing one pair with each of three hydrogen atoms, leaving one non-bonding pair; carbon dioxide has carbon sharing two pairs with each oxygen atom (two double bonds); every atom ends with a full outer shell.
caption: Figure: shared pairs in ammonia and carbon dioxide (outer shells only)

alt: Shell diagrams: lithium 2,1 has two occupied shells and one outer electron; aluminium 2,8,3 has three shells and three outer electrons; chlorine 2,8,7 has three shells and seven outer electrons. The number of shells gives the period and the outer electrons give the group.
caption: Figure: electrons in shells for lithium (2,1), aluminium (2,8,3) and chlorine (2,8,7)

alt: Fractional distillation apparatus: a flask of ethanol and water is heated below a fractionating column packed with glass beads; the thermometer at the top reads 78 degrees Celsius while ethanol, the lower-boiling liquid, reaches the top first, passes into the Liebig condenser and is collected, while water (100 degrees Celsius) condenses in the column and runs back.
caption: Figure: fractional distillation of ethanol and water

alt: Giant covalent structures: in diamond each carbon atom bonds to four others in a rigid three-dimensional network; in graphite each carbon bonds to three others in flat hexagonal layers, with only weak forces between the layers so they slide over each other.
caption: Figure: the structures of diamond and graphite

alt: Dot-and-cross diagrams: sodium transfers its one outer electron to chlorine, giving Na+ (outer shell of 8 crosses) and Cl- (8 outer electrons, 7 dots and 1 cross), formula NaCl; magnesium transfers two electrons to oxygen, giving Mg2+ and O2- each with a full outer shell, formula MgO.
caption: Figure: electron transfer in sodium chloride and magnesium oxide

alt: A slice through a sodium chloride lattice: smaller positive sodium ions and larger negative chloride ions alternate in rows and columns, each ion surrounded by ions of opposite charge, in the ratio 1 to 1.
caption: Figure: a layer of the giant ionic lattice of sodium chloride

alt: Metallic bonding: a regular lattice of positive metal ions surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons that are free to move; when a force is applied, layers of ions slide over each other while the electrons still hold the structure together, so the metal bends instead of shattering.
caption: Figure: positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, and layers sliding

alt: Filtration apparatus: a mixture of sand and salt solution is poured into a filter paper cone in a funnel; the insoluble sand stays on the paper as the residue and the salt solution runs through into the conical flask as the filtrate.
caption: Figure: filtration separates an insoluble solid (residue) from a liquid (filtrate)

alt: Simple distillation apparatus: salt solution is heated in a flask with a thermometer bulb level with the side arm; steam passes into a Liebig condenser with cold water entering at the bottom and leaving at the top, and pure water (distillate) drips into a beaker while the salt stays in the flask.
caption: Figure: simple distillation separates a solvent from a solution

alt: Solubility curve of potassium nitrate: solubility rises from 13.3 g per 100 g of water at 0 degrees Celsius to 31.6 g at 20 degrees and 110 g at 60 degrees, so cooling a saturated solution from 60 to 20 degrees crystallises 78.4 g per 100 g of water.
caption: Figure: solubility of potassium nitrate in water against temperature

alt: Titration set-up: acid in a burette with a tap above a conical flask holding 25.0 cm3 of alkali and a few drops of indicator, standing on a white tile so the end-point colour change is easy to see.
caption: Figure: titration apparatus
